Name: Humanoid
Description:
In a world where artificial intelligence opens up new horizons, our faith in its potential unveils a new outlook where, together, humans and machines build a new future filled with knowledge, inspiration, and incredible discoveries.

The development of a functional humanoid robot underpins an era of abundance and well-being where poverty will disappear, and people will be able to choose what they want to do.

We can imagine millions of bipedal robots doing more work than all human labour does today freeing people from the servitude of some repetitive and boring tasks that nobody likes to perform.

We believe that we have enough abundance to take care of everyone who is displaced. Eventually, providing a universal basic income will lead to the true evolution of our civilization.

Labor shortages loom, as the demands on our built environment rise. With the world’s workforce increasingly moving away from undesirable tasks, the manufacturing, construction, and logistics industries critical to our daily lives are left exposed.

By deploying our general-purpose humanoid robots in environments deemed hazardous or monotonous, we envision a future where human well-being is safeguarded while closing the gaps in critical global labour needs.

Description: Welcome to the Personal and Interactive Autonomous Systems (PaInt) Laboratory at Concordia! Our goal is to develop AI systems that seamlessly integrate with and support people in their dynamic environments over the long term. Towards this goal, one of the core problems that we work on is long-term personalization through a bi-directional relationship between AI agents (such as robots, autonomous vehicles, LLMs, recommender systems, etc.) and their users. In this relationship, users can continually interact with and teach AI agents about their individual preferences and unique environments, and these agents can provide long-term personalized assistance to the users by reasoning on the continually acquired knowledge. Our lab's expertise spans robotics, human-robot interaction, machine learning, computer vision, artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, and cognitive science. Name: Treloxai
Description:
We are a Physical AI company focused on perceiving, understanding, and reasoning about risk in the real world, especially the risks that are hardest to see.
We solve real operational and financial problems by revealing hidden hazards such as leaks, pooling liquids, glare, and transparent or reflective surfaces. These conditions escape conventional AI but drive incidents, downtime, and insurance losses.

We help operators reduce incidents and outages, insurers move from static assessments to continuous, trusted risk insight, and public-sector and defence stakeholders strengthen safety, resilience, and situational awareness.
Our vision is to make physical risk readable. To achieve this, we are building the Physical Risk Graph: a continuously evolving model of how hazards form, move, and matter inside real environments. It fuses video, thermal, depth, and other lightweight sensor data, often from existing infrastructure, with physics-aware reasoning to transform raw events into finance-grade risk signals in real time.
Our goal is simple: make hidden risks visible and bankable.

Name: Mirsee Robotics Inc.
Description:
Mirsee Robotics builds humanoid robots to solve manufacturing's labour crisis.
We've been developing humanoids since 2016 and have completed three humanoid generations. We design and build from the ground up, here in Cambridge, Ontario.

Here are some common questions we get from manufacturers about humanoid deployment:

Q: What problems do humanoids solve that arms, AMRs, and fixtures can't?
A: Fixed arms can manipulate parts, but can't move between stations. AMRs navigate a facility, but can't pick up a tote or place a part in a fixture. Fixtures automate one step, in one position, always. Humanoids handle tasks that require both navigation and manipulation, in spaces built for people.

Q: Is humanoid adoption about labour shortage, throughput, quality, safety, flexibility, or all of the above? How will we measure humanoid-deployment success?
A: The primary driver is labour shortage, specifically the roles with 80–100% annual turnover that companies can't consistently staff. When a role is reliably filled, throughput and safety improves as a result. The KPIs that matter most are turnover reduction in targeted roles, injury rate in those cells, output consistency across shifts, and onboarding cost savings. If those four numbers improve over a 180-day pilot, the business case for scaling is clear.

Q: Will humanoids replace our workers?
A: Not when deployed correctly. At Mirsee, we’re filling roles with high annual turnover: bin picking, tote handling, repetitive sorting. These aren't jobs people are fighting to keep, nor are they jobs that humans should have to do. When a humanoid fills one of these jobs, your people can move to work that requires human judgment and skill.

Q: Are Mirsee robots ready to deploy?
A: Not yet. We're in an active pilot phase inside Eclipse Automation's manufacturing facility; validating autonomous capabilities, stress-testing safety protocols, and building integration frameworks and repeatable deployment models manufacturers will need.

Name: Active & Interactive Robotics Lab

We analyze the interaction from physical aspects (e.g. maintaining physical safety and user ergonomics) and social aspects (e.g. perception, acceptance, ethics). In particular, we are interested in using these aspects within the control of the robots so that they can perform their tasks actively and efficiently, while being socially acceptable.

Our ultimate goal is to have robots seamlessly and intelligently interact with people in diverse environments including but not limited to manufacturing, home (e.g. cooking, cleaning), and long-term care institutions. Name: UBC Okanagan Marine Robotics
Description:
We're thrilled to introduce Okanagan Marine Robotics at UBC Okanagan. If you're as passionate about marine technology as we are, this club is your next port of call. We have two main focus areas: Electric Propulsion Boats and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles. This is the first and only club at UBCO dedicated to autonomous vehicles! We compete in various competitions such as the Monaco Energy Boat Challenge, Toronto Solar Boat Race, American Society of Naval Engineers for the Electric Propulsion Boat team, and RoboSub for the AUV team.

1. Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs):

This team is preparing to compete at the RoboSub competition by navigating through different levels of underwater obstacles. These obstacles include tasks such as shooting torpedoes, grabbing objects, dropping markers, and much more, testing the skills of our multidisciplinary team.

Join the Voyage:
Chat with us at Okanagan Marine Robotics, where your ideas can set sail!

Name: Avalon Robotics Inc
Description:
We help frontline teams in healthcare, hospitality, and beyond work smarter, not harder.

Too often, staff are overwhelmed with repetitive, non-core tasks like supply runs and cross-floor deliveries. This leads to burnout, low job satisfaction, and high turnover.

Our intelligent service robots seamlessly integrate into your team, taking on the heavy, time-consuming tasks, so your staff can focus on what truly matters: caring for people and delivering exceptional service.

We engineer, deploy, and support service bots for delivery, cleaning, material handling, and disinfection, boosting productivity, reducing burnout, and strengthening team morale.

Proudly Canadian. 

Building a Future Where People and Technology Thrive Together.

Technology That Cares. Innovation That Works.

Join Us.
Location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada

Name: movwize
Description: movwize is dedicated to bringing robotic intelligence to everyone. Building off our unique approach to motion planning, we build modules that bring robots into the AI era. Robots running movwize are more reliable, more intuitive, and more capable.

Name: Toronto Autonomous Systems Collective
Description: Welcome to the battleground of innovation at TMU. Where creativity meets technology in the ultimate showdown.

Name: ZELLIPS
Description:
Industrial player and specialist in timber construction, we support Canadian and international companies in their industrial transformation: from Lean Manufacturing and robotic integration to full production line automation.

How? Through mastery of industrial processes, minimizing preproduction errors, and optimizing resources.

Innovative for the timber sector while inspired by proven applications in various industrial fields, Zellips Group has developed a unique, cross-functional approach and proprietary technology based on BIM integration to synchronize information flows between business software and digital data transmitted to robots.

This industrial excellence, applied to timber construction, relies on teams of industry experts who guide you throughout the industrial transformation process:
 Organizational intelligence driven by Lean Manufacturing specialists to identify productivity gains in your factory, and adopt methods and tools efficiently
 Digital and robotic intelligence to deliver a customized, automated, and robotic production line: Smart Factory 4.0

This technology is continuously supported by the group’s R&D teams to ensure ongoing optimization and adaptability for each company and region.

This seamless model, already proven in France, meets strict construction standards and is expanding in North America and Africa.

 Need to move your production lines? Have an industrial transformation project ?
 We guide you every step of the way to unlock your full potential!
The company is based in France and Canada, serving international clients.

Name: WatDig
Description:
WatDig is a University of Waterloo Student Team part of the Sedra Student Design Centre and is currently entering our first year of competition in the Not-A-Boring Competition, hosted by The Boring Company.

This year we will be participating in the Navigation Challenge, where teams are tasked with creating an autonomous machine capable of computing and executing an optimized route through a maze of obstacles and checkpoints. The competition will consist of several design briefings and a final week long event in The Boring Company’s manufacturing and testing facility in Bastrop, Texas.

Name: Queen's Knights Robotics Team
Description: Queen's Knights Robotics Team is a student-run robotics team at Queen's University that designs, assembles, and programs 3 robots to compete in the ARC Robotics competition (formerly known as Robomaster). The team competed at the ARC Robotics Championship in 2026 and placed 5th globally in the 1v1 category and 7th globally in the 3v3 category, out of 24 teams. They also competed in the 2024 International North America Robomaster Competition and placed 5th among 25 teams. The team focuses on fostering technical excellence in mechanical, electrical, and software engineering, operating an excellent business and marketing team, and creating a closely-knit culture of passionate students where collaboration, innovation, and teamwork is central to our philosophy.

Name: Parchol
Description: Parchol is revolutionizing Robotics with AI-Driven Precision. We provide engineering solutions by consulting for robotics companies.

Name: UA-RAD
Description: UA-RAD is a student-led engineering team at the University of Alberta designing, building, and testing advanced unmanned aerial systems. We blend expertise in power systems, custom PCBs, sensor integration, and autonomous control to create high-performance, reliable drones for complex missions. Our goal: push UAS technology forward through innovation, teamwork, and hands-on engineering.

Name: aQuatonomous
Description:
aQuatonomous, derived from the words "aqua," "Queen’s," and "autonomous," is an innovative design team within Smith Engineering at Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario, Canada.

We are dedicated to conceptualizing, constructing, and programming an autonomous surface vessel (ASV/robotic boat) to compete annually in the RoboNation RoboBoat Competition.

Name: McMaster Exoskeleton
Description: The McMaster Exoskeleton Team is a student-led initiative affiliated with the McMaster Engineering Society. Our goal is to apply our degrees to develop a wearable lower-body robotic suit designed to augment the user's strength and mobility. We are committed to enhancing human mobility and strength through innovative exoskeleton systems.

Name: BoisBotics Inc.
Description: We have been in the industry for over 25 years. Our specialty lies with ABB system (from S4 all the way to the new Omnicore). We have experience in all aspects from mechanical, electrical and programming. We are open to assist in all aspects and look forward to helping our customers stay operational, as well as grow into the future.

Name: University of Toronto Autonomous Drone Racing (ADR) Team
Description: We are a University of Toronto robotics team of passionate roboticists, drone enthusiasts, and engineering students. Focused on revolutionizing drone racing with AI, we compete in international events, including the 2025 A2RL Challenge in Abu Dhabi, where drones autonomously navigate gates. Operating at the Flight Systems & Control Lab and Learning Systems & Robotics Lab, we use advanced tools like motion capture systems, 3D printers, and GPU tech. Join us in advancing the future of autonomous drones!

Name: Nabik Automations Inc.
Description: Nabik Automations Inc. is building the most agile robot for the ship maintenance and inspection industry in the world. Contact us at: contactnabik@gmail.com

Name: University of Manitoba Robotics Team
Description: The University of Manitoba Robotics Team (UMRT) is a student-driven engineering group that designs and builds advanced robotic systems to compete in events such as the Canadian International Rover Challenge (CIRC). Bringing together talent from mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering as well as computer vision, embedded systems, and communications, UMRT fosters hands-on innovation and collaboration. In addition to competition, the team is dedicated to growing the robotics community through workshops, outreach initiatives, and open competitions that inspire the next generation of engineers.

Name: UBC Subbots
Description:
UBC SubBots is an Engineering Student Team founded in 2017 dedicated to the development of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV). Subbots was founded as a collaboration between UBC Snowbots(now rover) and UBC SUBC. UBC Snowbots is a team dedicated to the research, education and development of autonomous systems, and SUBC is a team that focuses on the design and fabrication of human powered submarines. 

By leveraging each teams' expertise, SubBots is offering the UBC Engineering Community a new avenue to explore previously separated fields, bringing together students from a broad range of disciplines. Subbots' goal is to attend the annual Robosub competition in San Diego, California.

Name: EcoMarine Technologies Inc.
Description:
We build autonomous eco-friendly robots that clean and inspect under water surfaces such as ship hulls, fish pens, power dams, and wind towers. 

Our ROV is the perfect tool for under water maintenance, cleaning, and inspection.

Biofouling from ships can damage ecosystems, damage equipment, and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions by increasing fossil fuel consumption. 

We intend to change that by offering a cost-effective, easy, and highly available solution to entice ship owners into more frequent hull cleanings. 

By removing and capturing fouling from surface our ROV offers an invasive species prevention and remediation solution.

Name: Handi-Fuel
Description:
At Handi-Fuel, our mission is to empower people by understanding and eliminating barriers of entry leading to universally inclusive experiences. 

We understand the unique challenges faced by individuals with disabilities, and we are committed to enhancing their independence and improving their daily lives.

Name: Finite Robotics
Description: Based in uWaterloo's Velocity Innovation Arena, Finite Robotics is developing orchard robotics to help growers produce abundant, affordable, and delicious food.

Name: McMaster RoboSub
Description: McMaster RoboSub Team is a technical team at McMaster University focused on designing, building, and testing an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV). This AUV will compete in the annual RoboSub competition hosted by RoboNation. The competition consists of challenging teams to build an AUV capable of completing complex underwater tasks which include but are not limited to, obstacle navigation, torpedo deployment, and sample collection. The McMaster RoboSub team provides students with a hands-on application of interdisciplinary engineering fields, including Electrical, Mechanical, and Software Engineering. The RoboSub team is actively seeking financial support, guidance, and sponsorships to help fund the team. The financial support will be quintessential to funding the development of the AUV and help to cover competition-related expenses. Guidance will help to ensure that our designs are correct and effective. The sponsorships will aid in gaining development and testing facilities. A partnership with our club would provide sponsors with visibility among a highly motivated and technically skilled group of students, while also fostering innovation and hands-on learning experiences for future engineers. We welcome any assistance that can help propel our team toward success in the RoboSub competition.

Name: IntRoLab
Description:
IntRoLab est un laboratoire de recherche qui étudie, développe, intègre et utilise des méthodologies en mécatronique et en intelligence artificielle pour la conception de systèmes autonomes et intelligents. Les activités touchent différents champs de recherche portant sur la conception matérielle et logicielle de systèmes robotisés, embarqués et intelligents, ainsi qu'à l'évaluation de ces systèmes dans leur milieu d'opération. Les recherches menées au laboratoire sont qualifiées de pragmatiques, dans le sens qu'ils s'attaquent aux défis pour amener les robots et les systèmes intelligents à être utilisés en pratique dans le but d'améliorer la qualité de vie de la société, et du même coup découvrir les mystères liés à la création d'une intelligence sur des machines. Nos champs d'application sont les robots de services, les robots tout-terrains, les robots interactifs, la robotique d'assistance, la télésanté robotisée, l'automobile et les robots chirurgicaux.

IntRoLab is a research laboratory pursuing the goal of studying, developing, integrate and using mechatronics and artificial intelligence methodologies for the design of autonomous and intelligent systems. Research activities involve software and hardware design of mobile robots, embedded systems and autonomous agents, and in-situ evaluation. Research conducted at the lab is pragmatic, oriented toward overcoming the challenges associated with making robots and intelligent systems usable in real life situations to improve quality of life, and also discover how to give intelligence to machines. Application areas are service robots, all-terrain robots, interactive robots, assistive robotics, telehealth robotics, automobile and surgical robots.

Name: Umia Beauty
Description:
Umia is redefining the beauty industry with an AI-powered nail painting robot that delivers precision nail art and efficiency like never before. Designed for seamless self-serve use, Umia empowers nail artists and businesses globally to provide high-quality, consistent results to consumers. 

Launched with years of dedicated research, Umia brings a modern aesthetic and user-friendly technology to businesses worldwide, allowing nail artistry to become an accesible luxury to consumer, and enabling nail artists to work more effectively and expand their reach. 

Connect with us to learn more about how Umia is revolutionizing beauty tech.

Name: Viggen Robotics
Description: Viggen Robotics is building advanced Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) for landmine detection, unearthing, and identification. Our mission is to help reclaim and restore hazardous land through innovative robotic technologies that reduce human risk and improve operational safety. As an OEM, we combine modern engineering, decentralized manufacturing, and rapid prototyping to develop rugged, capable rover platforms for real-world deployment.

Name: Drimkoe
Description:
Drimkoe helps teams make defensible automation decisions before capital, credibility, or time is committed.

We work upstream of integration and execution—bringing clarity to feasibility, risk, and economics so automation initiatives can move forward with confidence, or stop early when they shouldn’t proceed.

Our approach combines:

Virtual-first analysis and simulation at appropriate fidelity

Selective grounding using real-world constraints and data

Clear requirements and acceptance criteria for partner execution

Drimkoe is vendor-neutral by design and partner-first in delivery. We don’t sell hardware or integration services—we focus on the decision layer that determines whether automation succeeds or fails.

Who we work with:

Manufacturers evaluating automation investments

System integrators seeking cleaner upstream scope

Robotics and automation startups validating deployments

What we believe:
Automation should be a calculated decision, not a leap of faith.

Name: Roboserve Canada
Description:
PROVIDING ROBOTIC SOLUTIONS TO:
Restaurants, Hotels, Schools, Libraries, Museums, Movie Theater, Hospitals and Senior Homes.

Name: Carleton Planetary Robotics Team
Description:
The Carleton Planetary Robotics Team (CPRT) is a student-led organization at Carleton University in Ottawa, Canada, dedicated to designing, building, and competing with Mars rovers in international robotics competitions.

Our team is made up of passionate undergraduates from the Faculty of Engineering and Design and the Faculty of Science. We thrive on collaboration, diversity, and a shared love of space exploration and robotics. 

Interested in joining us or supporting our mission? We invite new members and sponsors to connect with us and become part of the future of space exploration.

Name: HEAT Robotics
Description:
HEAT Robotics, an engineering student design team of IEEE UBCO Student Branch that conducts research and development on robotic applications in wildfires. Our team is made up of students from multiple disciplines that are passionate about utilizing robotics to solve global problems in innovative ways.

Our flagship product EMBR (Ember Mitigation Bot Responder) is an autonomous robotic system designed to address the critical challenge of managing and extinguishing residual embers post-wildfire. EMBR leverages advanced sensing technologies and AI-driven analysis to navigate through affected terrains, accurately detect hidden hotspots, and efficiently execute extinguishing protocols. This innovative approach not only enhances firefighting efforts but also significantly reduces the risk of re-ignition, contributing to safer, more effective wildfire recovery operations.

Name: AstroMean Inc.
Description: AstroMean Inc. is an applied AI research lab in Toronto focused on building intelligence layer for robotics. Our work is inspired heavily by the human brain.

Name: UniRobotic
Description: Master distributor for Canada ( Ontario - Quebec - Eastern Canada ) for Elite Robots

Name: Orbital
Description:
Orbital develops a novel high efficient and durable reducer technology for e-bikes and robotic applications
The innovative technology developed by Orbital greatly simplifies the gear mechanism and eliminates all friction movements between the different elements. These innovations have the potential to significantly increase gear life while ensuring exceptional efficiency.
Orbital aims to make a better use of energy for a sustainable environment.

Name: Subvision Robotics Inc.
Description: At Subvision Robotics, we are revolutionizing marine maintenance with autonomous, eco-friendly solutions. Our mission is to develop innovative robotics that prevent biofouling at its source, enhancing vessel efficiency, reducing fuel consumption, and protecting marine ecosystems.

Name: Mechatronic and Robotic Systems Laboratory
Description: The Mechatronic and Robotic Systems (MARS) Laboratory at Ontario Tech University performs research in the areas of mechatronics, robotics and automation, and optimal design. In particular the lab focuses on the application of advanced kinematics for the control of redundant manipulator systems including joint redundant arms, redundantly-actuated parallel manipulators, and mobile-manipulator systems. The Director of the MARS Laboratory is Professor Scott Nokleby.

Name: make87
Description:
make87 is the unified platform for building, deploying, and scaling Physical AI—robots, smart machines, and AI-enabled devices that sense and act in the real world.
Teams model distributed applications visually, connect edge devices to cloud services in minutes, and manage entire fleets with real-time observability and over-the-air updates. We handle the hard stuff—networking, orchestration, security, and lifecycle management—so you can focus on application logic and ship production systems in days, not months.

Why we exist:
Physical AI is still in its infancy. Our mission is to power its emergence by making it so accessible that anyone can build and deploy it—removing six-figure infrastructure costs and months of bespoke engineering.

Who we serve:
• Established robotics and automation companies expanding or modernizing their fleets
• New entrants exploring AI-driven products without prohibitive upfront spend
• R&D teams needing a reproducible path from prototype to global rollout

Founded in 2024, privately held, with a distributed team in Canada and Germany.

Name: Polymorph
Description: At Polymorph, we see a universal truth: humanity's greatest ideas are often bottlenecked by our physical limitations. We are building general purpose humanoid robots as the ultimate tool to bridge the gap between digital intelligence and physical work. These machines are physical platforms for intelligence, providing an embodied form for AI to learn, adapt, and interact with the complex, dynamic environments we inhabit. Our name is our thesis: a single, versatile body that can polymorph its function through software, mastering an ever-expanding library of skills. Our mission is to unbind human potential from physical constraints, amplifying the capacity of creators, scientists, and caregivers to solve the world's most important challenges. We are building the ultimate toolmaker, so humanity can become the ultimate maker of meaning.

Name: OBotz Robotics & Coding
Description:
OBotz is a Canada based multidisciplinary robotics program with a specially designed curriculum to teach young children about robotics. STEM learning is the building block of this program allowing children to think scientifically and evolve technically.

The program utilizes hands-on activities to engage a child’s curious mind. Children learn to experiment, innovate and build robotic models and machines throughout the 7 progressive levels of this course.

Name: NIO Robotics
Description:
NIO Robotics is a Canadian startup that designs advanced robotic solutions to automate the most demanding tasks in complex environments.
By combining mobile, agile, and collaborative robotics with sophisticated engineering, NIO Robotics develops high-performance, reliable systems tailored to the most rigorous industrial applications.

Name: Kelpie Robotics
Description:
(Le français suit)
We are Kelpie Robotics, an ambitious engineering design team from the University of Ottawa. Nestled within the innovative John McIntyre Team Space, our mission is to cultivate hands-on learning experiences for students passionate about making a tangible impact on the world.

As annual contenders in the MATEROV competition, we specialize in constructing underwater robots—ROVs designed to tackle pressing global challenges like climate change, renewable energy, and ocean conservation. 

Proud participants in the 2022 and 2023 World Championships in Long Beach, California, and Longmont, Colorado, we're now setting our sights on the 2025 World Championships in Alpena, Michigan. Our presence at the University of Ottawa isn't just about participation; it's about making a mark. Our leadership roles embody our entrepreneurial spirit—each position, from CEO, COO to CTO, represents our commitment to innovation and excellence.

Influenced by the spirit of MATEROV, we foster entrepreneurial skills that distinguish us from the crowd. Furthermore, we integrate a comprehensive ESG analysis into our workflow, underscoring our dedication to responsible engineering and sustainable development.

Join us as we dive deeper. #watergame
--
Nous sommes Kelpie Robotics, une équipe de conception en génie de l’Université d’Ottawa basée à l’espace de collaboration John McEntyre. Notre mission : offrir aux étudiants des expériences pratiques à impact réel.

Chaque année, nous participons au concours MATE ROV, en construisant des robots sous-marins pour répondre à des enjeux mondiaux comme le climat, l’énergie durable et la préservation des océans.

Après avoir fièrement représenté l’Université aux championnats du monde en 2022 et 2023, nous visons maintenant Alpena 2025. Du PDG au CTO, notre leadership incarne innovation, excellence et esprit entrepreneurial.

Portés par l’esprit MATEROV, nous intégrons une analyse ESG pour une ingénierie responsable.

Plongez avec nous.

Name: CTA CNC Inc
Description:
Fondée en 2013, CTA CNC a commencé dans la maintenance industrielle avant d’évoluer vers l’intégration de technologies avancées et solutions automatisées. Aujourd’hui, notre équipe accompagne les entreprises manufacturières dans leur transformation industrielle.

Vous trouverez chez CTA CNC un ensemble de services et de marchandises qui nous permettent de répondre à tous vos besoins de robotisation et d'usinage. 

•	Diamond Partner, Système intégrateur Mitsubishi Electric Automation 
•      Conception de cellule robotisée pour machine-outil et presse-pliage
•	Distributeur Castrol Industriel
•	Distributeur Grundfos Industriel
•	Distributeur/Intégrateur Renishaw
•	Analyse de lubrifiants en laboratoire
•	Vente d’équipements CNC 
•	Achat de machine-outil usagée

Name: Ontario Tech Exoskeleton Design Team (EXOTU)
Description:
EXOTU is Ontario Tech University’s official Exoskeleton Engineering Design Team.

We are a student-led engineering design team dedicated to creating wearable robotic exoskeletons that enhance human mobility and physical performance. Our projects explore applications across diverse industries, including medical rehabilitation, athletics, industrial support, and even extreme environments such as deep-water exploration. By working at the intersection of innovation and human capability, we aim to push the boundaries of wearable robotics while training the next generation of engineers.

What makes EXOTU unique is our interdisciplinary approach. Our team brings together students from mechanical, electrical, software, and related engineering fields to collaborate on challenging, real-world projects. Members gain hands-on experience in design, prototyping, testing, and systems integration. Skills that go far beyond the classroom and directly prepare them for careers in emerging technologies.

Beyond technical expertise, EXOTU fosters a strong community built on teamwork, leadership, and collaboration. We provide opportunities for professional development, industry networking, and participation in design competitions. Through these experiences, our members grow not only as engineers but also as innovators, problem-solvers, and leaders.

As Ontario Tech’s exoskeleton design team, we strive to showcase the university’s commitment to cutting-edge innovation while building technologies that can make a meaningful impact on society.

Name: Speedbot North America
Description:
With over 100 patents and patent pending, Speedbot provides AI + 3D vision metrology/measurement, inspection and motion control solutions for automotives, heavy industry, logistics and general manufacturing companies.  

Speedbot was founded by scientists with multiple research achievements in 3D vision, robotics, 3D graphics, network computing and big data. 

With its worldwide operations in Europe, Asia and North America, Speedbot employs over 350 people, most of which hold master’s degrees or higher from leading institutions such as Princeton University, Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, Bonn University of Germany and Columbia University.

Name: FRC Team 1325: Inverse Paradox
Description: Established in 2004 FIRST Robotics Competition Team 1325 Inverse Paradox is a community robotics team located in Mississauga, Ontario. Our mission is to follow the values of FIRST and promote a team environment in which an interest of science, technology and innovation will be fostered in and enjoyed by students, parent volunteers and others members of the community. Our team consists of over 50 high school students from grades 9 to 12 working together to build a 120 pound robot.

Name: Umoja Robotics
Description: Canada's First African-Canadian Youth Robotics Team. We inspire Black youth to succeed in STEM careers.

Name: Declix Solutions Inc.
Description: Declix Solutions is a designer, manufacturer, and supplier of robotic products for the manufacturing and aerospace industries. We create equipment that enhance the autonomy of drones and have industrial automation capabilities.
